# Levels

> Levels is a free, open source (MIT) macOS menu bar app that gives every app its own volume slider and mute button. It uses Apple's Core Audio process taps (macOS 14.2+), so it installs no drivers or kernel extensions. Install with `brew install rafaelisdev/tap/levels`.

Key facts:

- Platform: macOS 11 Big Sur and later, universal app (Apple Silicon and Intel), 0.8 MB download.
- Per-app volume and mute need macOS 14.2 or later. On older systems Levels controls the output device volume only.
- Languages: the interface follows the Mac's language: English, Spanish, German, French, Portuguese, Russian, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Korean.
- Permission: macOS asks once for "System Audio Recording Only". Audio is processed locally in real time and is never recorded, stored or uploaded.
- If Levels quits or crashes, every app immediately returns to its normal volume.
- Levels remembers each app's volume and applies it again whenever that app plays.
- Price: free. License: MIT. Source code: https://github.com/rafaelisdev/levels
- Current version: 1.3. Formerly named VolumeMixer.
- Not yet supported: sending sound to two outputs at once (in development), per-app EQ or effects.

## Install

- Homebrew: `brew install rafaelisdev/tap/levels` (update with `brew upgrade levels`, remove with `brew uninstall --zap levels`)
- Script: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafaelisdev/levels/main/install.sh | bash` (downloads the latest release, verifies its SHA-256, installs to /Applications)
- Manual: download Levels.zip from https://github.com/rafaelisdev/levels/releases/latest. The app is not notarized, so macOS blocks the first launch until you click "Open Anyway" in System Settings > Privacy & Security.
